title.narrative: Supporting Fourth Primary Education Development Program

description.narrative: The Fourth Primary Education Development Program will support Bangladesh's primary education system to become an efficient and effective system that provides quality primary education to all Bangladeshi children. The new program will build on the achievements of previous programs with a strong focus on strengthening quality of education, improving access to education, and enhancing institutional management through decentralization. The new program is aligned with the country partnership strategy, 2016-2020 which indicates Asian Development Bank's continued support to primary education.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Quality of primary education improved Indicator: At least 50% of the target for training teachers and teacher educators in the CPD plan achieved (at least 50% of them women) (2017 baseline: 0. 2022 update: 28% of CPD training target achieved) (OP 2.1.1; OP 6.2.1) Progress/Status: Achieved. Total of 384,513 (female: 251,782 and male: 132,731) teachers are working in Government primary schools (GPSs). Out of the total teachers 383,700 (female: 251,324 and male: 132,376) teachers and 2,010 officers/educators have received at least one of the trainings (curriculum dissemination training) conducted (around 95%) under the approved CPD implementation plan. (Source: JARM 2024). Data Source: DPE report based on EMIS and/or ASPR
Actual value:

Output: Governance and management or primary education system improved Indicator: 80% of approved contracts (goods and works) in DPE processed through e-GP in the year (2017 baseline: e-GP initiated at DPE. 2022 update: target fully achieved) (OP 6.1.4) Progress/Status: Achieved. 100% of approved contracts (goods and works) in DPE processed through e-GP. (Source: DPE report, 8 September 2024).
Data Source: DPE procurement progress report Actual value:

Output: Governance and management or primary education system improved Indicator: At least 90% of DPE's division, district, and upazila level drawing and disbursing officers adopted iBAS++ (2017 baseline: iBAS++ introduced in DPE. 2022 update: target fully achieved) (OP 6.1.4) Progress/Status: Achieved. iBAS++ has been rolled out in 100% of all DDOs for the submission of pay bill. Of all DDOs, 90% have been currently preparing budget through iBAS++. (Source: RoD of 6th JCM held on 23 November 2021). Data Source: MOPME report on PEDP4 progress Actual value:

Output: Access and participation to primary education enhanced Indicator: Additional 43,500 gender-segregated WASH blocks, 11,250 safe drinking water sources, and 30,000 classrooms completed according to the Infrastructure Planning Guideline of MOPME and as per standard of the Bangladesh National Building Code (2017 baseline: 24,338 WASH blocks; 39,348 water sources; and 39,003 classrooms completed during the PEDP3. 2022 update: 13,212 WASH blocks; 9,068 water sources; and 9,134 classrooms completed during PEDP4) (OP 1.3.1; 2.1.4) Progress/Status: Partially achieved and Ongoing. 32,393 additional classrooms were completed. So, 32,393 out of 40,000 is approximately 81% completed.
43,868 gender-segregated WASH blocks were completed. So, 43,868 out of 58,000 is approximately 76% completed. All completed WASH blocks fully comply with gender-segregated design standards and include disability-friendly features, ensuring inclusivity and accessibility for all students.
16,682 safe drinking water sources were installed. So, 16,682 out of 11,250 is approximately 149% completed. Additionally, 100% of respondents reported that their school provides a safe drinking water supply.
All completed infrastructure (additional classrooms, gender-segregated WASH blocks, and drinking water sources) fully complies with IPG and BNBC standards. (Source: DPE report, 22 April 2025, RoD of 12 JCM, 5 February 2025). Data Source: EMIS and/or ASPR Actual value:

Output: Access and participation to primary education enhanced Indicator: Additional 3,000 government schools converted from double-shift to single-shift operations (2017 baseline: 22.6% of existing government schools have single-shift operations. 2020 update: additional 745, or 2% of government schools converted to single-shift) (OP 6.2.1) Progress/Status: Achieved. • In 2017, 9,112 single-shift schools were operational out of 38,879 government primary schools (GPS) as per APSC 2017). • In 2023, 12,515 single-shift schools were operational out of 65,565 government primary schools (GPS) as per APSC 2023). • Additional 3403 single-shift schools were operational in PEDP4 period. • Over the period, 19.09% of government primary schools converted from double shift to single shift. (Source: APSC 2023 and RoD of 12 JCM, 5 February 2025).
Data Source: EMIS and/or ASPR Actual value:

Output: Access and participation to primary education enhanced Indicator: Additional 650,000 out-of-school children enrolled in learning centers (50% boys) (2017 baseline: 100,072 [50% boys]. 2022 update: additional 583,893 enrolled [52% boys]) (OP 1.1.1) Progress/Status: Achieved. A total of 802,536 out-of-school children (388,157 girls and 414,379 boys) are enrolled in 33,334 learning centers (LCs) under PEDP4. (Source: ASPR 2022 and JARM 2024). Data Source: Bureau of Non-Formal Education endorsed implementation support agency report Actual value:

Output: Quality of primary education improved Indicator: 67,500 newly recruited and existing teachers without DPEd or CinEd (at least 50% of them women) certified through DPEd program (among them, 25,000 certified through updated DPEd program), and 1,200 teacher educators with capacity to deliver the updated DPEd program (2017 baseline: 32,353 teachers with DPEd. Not applicable as regards to training of teacher educators on DPEd. 2021 update: 46,696 teachers without DPEd or CinEd certified through DPEd) (OP 2.1.1; OP 6.2.1) Progress/Status: Achieved. A total of 76,891 newly recruited and existing teachers without DPEd or CinEd teachers received DPEd training, including 51,132 female (64%) and 25,759 male teachers. A total of 20,863 teachers and educators, comprising 13,223 females (63.38%) and 7,640 males, completed the 10-month Basic Training for Primary Teachers (BTPT)/revised DPEd curriculum. 1,781 teachers received C-in-Ed training. A total of 1,340 teacher educators are trained to effectively deliver the updated DPEd. (Source: NAPE, April 2025). Data Source: National Academy for Primary Education and/or DPE report, EMIS, ASPR Actual value:

Output: Quality of primary education improved Indicator: At least 50.0% of government primary schools meet the student-teacher ratio standard of 40:1 (2016 baseline: 35.4%. 2020 update: 78.3%) (OP 6.2.1) Progress/Status: Achieved. 80.05% (52,452) of government primary schools meet the student-teacher ratio standard of 40:1 or less. (Source: ASPR 2022-2023, Published March 2024; JARM 2024).
Data Source: ASPR Actual value:

Output: Quality of primary education improved Indicator: Revised pre-primary and grades 1-5 curricula and textbooks, and newly developed teaching-learning materials (with selected supplementary reading materials) approved by the National Curriculum Coordination Committee (2017 baseline: grades 1-5 curricula in 2011 version to be updated, and textbooks in 2013 version to be updated; teaching-learning materials, including supplementary reading materials, not made available to schools. 2022 update: Revised pre-primary and grades 1-5 curricula approved) (OP 6.2.1) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. • The National Curriculum and Textbook Board (NCTB) has developed and revised textbooks, teaching-learning materials (TLMs), and supplementary reading materials (SRMs) for preprimary and primary grades 1-5 followed based on the revised curriculum 2022 and revised curriculum 2021 respectively. • The MoPME formed the National Curriculum Coordination Committee (NCCC) for textbook approval through evaluation, and NCTB formed sub-committees and deployed writers in 2020 to develop the materials. • A 20-member National Curriculum Coordination Committee (NCCC), led by the Secretary of the MoPME, oversees this process. • A total of 20 (10 for 4+ PPE and 10 for 5+ PPE) storybooks for pre-primary and 10 story books for grades 1-5 have been developed by NCTB. Besides, a total of 173 story books as SRMs for grades 1-5 were identified by NCTB. NCTB held a national workshop to finalize textbooks, TLMs, and SRMs for pre-primary. Experimental textbooks for grades 1-3 were developed in 2023 and revised in October 2024. • NCTB approved experimental textbooks for pre-primary and grades 1-3. Textbooks for pre-primary by the NCCC in July 2023, and experimental textbooks for grades 1-3 were approved in 2023 and distributed in 2024, based on the revised 2021 curriculum. • The revised textbooks for grades 1-5 were approved by the NCCC in October 2024 and endorsed by MoPME in October 2024 as confirmed by a MoPME letter. MoPME also approved the revised textbooks for PPE in December 2024. • TLMs for pre-primary for grades 1-5 and SRMs for both pre-primary and grades 1-5 were completed, finalized and approved in October 2024. (Source: APSC 2023 and RoD of 12 JCM, 5 February 2025). Data Source: National Curriculum and Textbook report Actual value: Y

Output: Quality of primary education improved Indicator: Additional 100,750 teachers (at least 50% of them women) completed training on using ICT and e- teaching-learning resources through ICT training (2016 baseline: 71,862 teachers trained on ICT [men: 23,097; women: 48,765]. 2020 update: 30,805 teachers trained on ICT) (OP 2.1.1; OP 6.2.1) Progress/Status: Achieved. Additionally, a total of 383,700 (female: 251,324 and male: 132,376) teachers and 2,010 officers/educators have received online curriculum dissemination training. A total of 50,800 (female: 26420 and male: 24,380) teachers received ICT in Education training. (Source: DPE Report, 8 August 2024; and ASPR 2022-2023; JARM 2024). Data Source: DPE report based on EMIS and/or ASPR Actual value:

Output: Governance and management or primary education system improved Indicator: A need and performance-based UPEP piloted for 50 upazilas as per updated UPEP guidelines (2017 baseline: UPEP not funded. 2022 update: target fully achieved) (OP 6.1.1) Progress/Status: Achieved. UPEP guideline updated and approved by MoPME. It was piloted in 50 upazilas during the PEDP4 period. Data Source: UPEP implementation report Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Y Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Y Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: Governance and management or primary education system improved Indicator: Institutional strengthening plan as per the updated ODCBG implemented. (2017 baseline: ODCBG being updated. 2022 update: all activities of the plan initiated) (OP 6.1.1) Progress/Status: Partially Achieved and Ongoing. The Institutional Strengthening Plan (ISP) includes 36 recommended activities. As of JARM 2024 thirteen (13) activities have been fully achieved, 21 activities are ongoing, and 2 activities need further review. • Out of the ongoing activities DPE claimed that 5 activities related to the translation of job descriptions into Bangla, printing, and dissemination had been achieved. However, DPE will provide supporting evidence to ADB ISP Consultant to verify the progress of the activities. • The 2 activities related to the renaming were marked as "in need of further review." DPE officials emphasized the importance of these activities for strengthening the DPE structure and mentioned that they expect approval from MoPME by 30 April 2025. • A proposal had been made by DPE/MoPME to merge the creation of an additional 30,000 posts of Assistant Teachers (AT) with 65,593 posts of Assistant Head Teachers (AHT) as Ministry of Public Administration (MoPA) returned the proposal for the additional 30,000 were not required, as the newly created AHT positions (65,593) would become vacant through promotions and would be filled by recruiting ATs. As a result, the proposal for the additional 30,000 AT posts was dropped from the plan. The DPE will provide supporting evidence to verify the progress. (Source: DPE, ISP progress report, JARM 2024 and Summary of ISP Meeting on 25 March and RoD of ISP meeting, 8 April 2025). Data Source: MOPME report on PEDP4 progress Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Y Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Y Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: Governance and management or primary education system improved Indicator: Integrated web-based EMIS with sex-disaggregated data (including for social groups) made operational in DPE (2017 baseline: some EMIS subsystems exist but are not integrated and not web-based. 2022 update: integration ongoing and on track) (OP 2.3.2; OP 6.1.1) Progress/Status: Achieved. Six modules (APSC, Textbook, PECE, NSA, teacher database and student database) are integrated and the system is operated across each module. System-generated performance reports prepared by DPE which called the Integrated Primary Education Management Information System (IPEMIS). (Source: RVR report and 9th JCM).
Data Source: Integrated EMIS website, MOPME report Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Y Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Y Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: Governance and management or primary education system improved Indicator: Student number-based SLIP fund received by 85% of government schools in the year as per updated SLIP guidelines (2017 baseline: 0 [all government schools received flat SLIP fund within the PEDP3]. 2022 update: target fully achieved) (OP 6.1.1) Progress/Status: Achieved. 65,565 schools benefited from SLIP. 100% school received SLIP fund as per updated SLIP guidelines. Formula-based SLIP fund has been disbursed to all 65,565 GPS in last FY 2022-23. (Source: 8th JCM, 27 March 2023; DPE administrative data).
Data Source: SLIP implementation progress report Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Y Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: Y Target year: 2025 Target value: Y
Quality and equity of primary education improved for all children from pre-primary to grade 5

Proportion of grade 3 students with minimum proficiency in Bangla and mathematics increased by 10 percentage points for both boys and girls from the 2017 baseline (NSA 2017 baseline: Bangla - 47% [boys 45%, girls 48%]; and Math - 34% [boys 35%, girls 33%] (OP 1.1.1) Achievement: N Progress/Status: Partially achieved. 2022 NSA: Bangla - 51% [boys 47%, girls 55%]; and Math - 39% [boys 38%, girls 40%]. (Source: NSA 2022). Data Source: National Student Assessment Actual value: N

National survival rate to grade 5 increased by 2 percentage points for both boys and girls (2017 baseline: 83.3% [boys: 81.3%, girls: 85.4%]. 2020 update: 84.7% [Boys 83.3% and Girls 85.9%]) (OP 1.1.1) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. National survival rate to grade 5: 86.93% (Boys: 85.91%; Girls: 87.83%) in 2023. The survival rate is the percentage of a cohort of students enrolled in grade 1 who reach up to grade 5 in Bangladesh regardless of repetition. (Source: APSC 2023 and ASPR 2022-2023. Published in November 2024). Data Source: ASPR Actual value: Y

Difference in net enrollment rates in grades 1-5 between the weighted average of five lowest performing districts and the national level decreased to 7% (boys: 10%; girls: 4%) (2016 baseline: 9% [boys:12.5%; girls: 5.0%]. 2020 update: 4.7%). (OP 1.1.1) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. The difference in net enrollment rates for grades 1-5 between the weighted average of the five lowest-performing districts and the national level has reduced to 2.2% [boys: 2.4%; girls: 1.9%]., a significant improvement from the target of 7%. The 5 lowest-performing districts are Narsingdi, Jaypurhat, Pabna, Khagrachhari and Rangamati in 2021 and Bogura, Brahmanbaria, Kishoreganj, Sunamganj and Narail in 2022. This is linked to KPI-8. (Source: ASPR 2022-2023. Published in November 2024). Data Source: ASPR Actual value: Y
